scenario: Scenario 2: A TRSP detached by truncate's forced replacement keeps running unattached
notes: All five TargetSafe counterexamples (MC-1 to MC-5) were reproduced, each with the target exception thrown at AssignmentManager.java:769; the fields above give MC-3 as the representative because it needs no injected fault and leaves the region unserved. MC-3 chain: truncate takes the region lock; preTransitCheck does not consult that lock, so a move or balancer plan attaches a TRSP; truncate's forced unassign detaches the TRSP without stopping it and completes; the detached TRSP then writes CLOSING with no owner, the RegionServer's close report is dropped, and the next Admin.move, assign or unassign throws at line 769 while client I/O on the region fails. Evidence: a public-API race of Admin.move against truncateRegionAsync hit in 5 of 5 runs on a pristine export of 1790942bb2, and the counterexample's balancer path hit with only a timing hook on preTruncateRegionAction, on a two-RegionServer mini cluster; the no-move control stayed clean. The other reproduced findings use other mechanisms: MC-1 an operator abort racing split PREPARE, MC-2 a split/unassign race plus a namespace quota failure, MC-4 a decommission racing a split, and MC-5 a master failover with RSGroup enabled. The MC_hunt_forced_detach_scp configs found no violation, but only for one crash during one truncate and with the search cut by the MaxPid bound at both sizes. Code-review findings have no TargetSafe counterexample: CR-1, CR-4, CR-6, CR-8 and CR-12 were also reproduced firing the target line, CR-7 and CR-10 were reproduced without it, CR-3's unaided failure is at line 766, CR-2 and CR-11 are MASKED, and CR-5 and CR-9 are FALSE POSITIVE. A frame at line 769 alone does not show broken coordination: per CR-5, the unmodified workload test throws and catches it, contrary to the target file's note that the check does not fail there, so MC-3's confirmation rests on the ownerless CLOSING state as well as the frame.
